title: Standardize RFP response library structure, approvals, and ownership model
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Problem
Enterprise deals for Dedicated + Private are increasingly gated by formal RFPs/security questionnaires. We have good draft language across Drive/Slack/email, but it is not consistently discoverable, versioned, or clearly approved. This leads to:
- Inconsistent answers across AEs/SEs (especially on data residency, retention, audit logs, ISO language)
- Risk of over-committing ("roadmap" implied in responses)
- Slow turnaround on questionnaires due to unclear review/approval path
- No canonical place to cite in RFPs (hard to reference a version/date)

Goal
Define and implement a standardized RFP response library structure + an approval workflow + an ownership model across GTM, Security/GRC, and Legal so that:
- Sales/SE can self-serve 80%+ of responses using approved language
- Security/Legal can review changes efficiently with clear accountability
- We can reference specific, versioned language in RFP submissions
- Claims align with current product capabilities across Hosted/Dedicated/Private (no roadmap promises)

Non-goals
- Creating new security features/capabilities
- Rewriting every legacy questionnaire response immediately (focus on the top 20–30 control themes and the most common blockers)
- Publishing sensitive evidence publicly (SOC 2 report remains gated under NDA)

Proposed library structure (canonical)
Canonical location: Confluence (Sales Enablement → Security/Compliance). Drive remains the drafting workspace only.

1) RFP Response Library (page set)
- Index page with: purpose, usage instructions, last reviewed date, owners, and evidence request links
- Sections organized by domain (each section has short + long form answers):
  A. Company security program overview (policies, governance, training)
  B. Data protection & privacy (data use, training on customer data, DPA posture)
  C. Encryption & key management (in transit/at rest; KMS boundaries; Private options)
  D. Identity & access management (SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC granularity)
  E. Logging & monitoring (audit log taxonomy, retention, export options)
  F. Secure SDLC (SAST/DAST, dependency scanning, code review, CI/CD)
  G. Vulnerability management & penetration testing (approved phrasing + evidence path)
  H. Incident response & breach notification (process overview; contractual terms handled by Legal)
  I. Business continuity & disaster recovery (high-level posture)
  J. Subprocessors & third-party risk (where to find canonical list; review cadence)
  K. Deployment-mode specifics (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private shared responsibility)

2) “What we do and don’t say” guardrails
- Anti-claims and phrasing guardrails (e.g., ISO language, residency nuance, pen test frequency wording)
- Explicit “do not promise” list (roadmap; absolute guarantees; unsupported integrations)

3) Claims matrix linkage
- Every RFP block links to a claims-matrix row (or ID) indicating evidence availability and owner.

4) Snippet IDs for reuse
- Each answer block gets a stable snippet ID (e.g., RFP-IAM-SSO-001) for referencing in:
  - HubSpot snippets/templates
  - Internal admin snippet tool (see PR-39122)
  - Deal desk/CRM notes

Versioning + change control
- Versioning format: YYYY.MM (e.g., 2026.02). Each page shows: Version, Last reviewed date, Approvers.
- Change log page tracks: what changed, why, requester, approvers, and rollout notes.
- Sales instruction: cite the library version in RFP submissions when possible (e.g., “Response language sourced from Redwood RFP Library v2026.02”).

Approval workflow (operational)
1) Intake
- Change request originates from: (a) field ask (AE/SE), (b) support ticket trend, (c) product capability change, (d) compliance/audit update.
- Intake form (lightweight): requested change, reason, affected snippet IDs, requested due date, deal context (optional).

2) Drafting (GTM Ops / Program Mgmt)
- Draft in Drive using the master draft doc, mark changes with suggested edits.

3) Review (required)
- Security technical accuracy: Marcus Lin or Kevin Osei
- GRC/compliance posture language: Olga Petrov or Daniel Carter
- Product capability alignment / roadmap disclaimer: Naomi Feldman
- Legal review required when the block touches contractual commitments (e.g., breach notification timelines, limitations of liability, audit rights): Michael Grant

4) Approve + publish
- Approvals recorded on the Confluence page (Approver names + date) and in the change log.
- Publish to Confluence (canonical) and update HubSpot snippet references where applicable.

5) Exception path
- If a customer questionnaire asks for a control not supported:
  - Use the approved alternative language from the exceptions policy.
  - Escalate for approval if the ask implies product commitment or contractual deviation.

SLA targets
- Standard change request: 5 business days to approve/publish (assuming no Legal changes)
- Deal-critical (defined by Sales sponsor): 2 business days, requires explicit “deal-critical” flag and Security/GRC acknowledgment

RACI (proposed)
- Responsible (content maintenance): Security/GRC + Product Security PM (for accuracy), Program Manager (for process + publishing)
- Accountable (final content posture): CISO (Dr. Aisha Rahman) for security posture; Legal (Michael Grant) for contractual language
- Consulted: Solutions Engineering (Markus Klein / Fatima Noor / Colin O’Donnell), Product Marketing (Camila Reyes / Soojin Lee)
- Informed: Sales leadership (Jordan Blake), CS (Jasmine Liu / Rachel Kim)

Deliverables
- Confluence: RFP Response Library (indexed, sectioned, versioned)
- Confluence: Change log + versioning policy for RFP library (mirrors FAQ discipline)
- Drive: Locked “master draft” retained for history, but canonical is Confluence
- HubSpot/CRM: Mapping of snippet IDs to templates/snippets used by Sales

Acceptance criteria
- A Confluence index page exists with clear owners, SLA, and canonical links
- At least 30 approved answer blocks are published across the domains above
- Each block has: snippet ID, last reviewed date, deployment-mode caveats (where relevant), and evidence request link (where applicable)
- Approval rules documented and validated by Security/GRC + Legal (for applicable sections)
- Sales/SE training note added to enablement kit index page with “how to use/cite versions”

Risks / open questions
- Where to store “restricted” evidence references without leaking access paths (need to point to the evidence request playbook, not the folder)
- Keeping HubSpot snippets in sync with Confluence (need a single source of truth; likely Confluence → admin snippet tool)
- Region-specific residency statements must be carefully scoped (no blanket guarantees)

Links
- Enablement Kit umbrella: PM-4821
- Draft library bank (Drive): shared_drives/go-to-market/rfp-response-library-master-draft
- Claims matrix (Drive): shared_drives/security-and-compliance/security-claims-matrix
- RFP approvals SOP (Confluence): finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/rfp-response-ownership-and-approvals
- Exceptions policy (Confluence): security-and-compliance/risk-and-exceptions/customer-security-questionnaire-exceptions-policy
- Evidence request playbook (Confluence): security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence/soc2-customer-evidence-request-playbook
comments: 2026-01-10 (Talia Benson): Kicked off with Naomi + Markus. Key pain: each AE has their own “latest” blocks in email/Slack. Consensus that Confluence should be canonical; Drive stays draft-only.

2026-01-14 (Naomi Feldman): Added note that anything that sounds like a contractual commitment must be routed to Legal. We should avoid including specific breach notification timelines in the library unless Legal pre-approves language.
2026-01-18 (Olga Petrov): Strongly recommend snippet IDs and a change log. Also: do not say “ISO certified” unless we are. Approved wording should be “alignment” only with explicit caveat.

2026-01-22 (Marcus Lin): For pen test/vuln mgmt blocks: keep answers high-level and route evidence via the playbook. No claims about frequency in the library unless we can support consistently year over year.

2026-01-27 (Camila Reyes): Messaging request: include a short “shared responsibility model” paragraph per deployment mode and keep tone consistent with security FAQ (developer-first, production-grade, no fluff).

2026-02-03 (Michael Grant): Reviewed incident response and breach language sections. Approved adding a “process overview” block, but directed us to avoid any contract-specific numbers; point customers to Security Addendum/DPA process instead.

2026-02-07 (Markus Klein): Field feedback: audit log export questions are recurring. Suggest prioritizing the logging section and linking to docs PR once merged. Also need a Private deployment appendix-style block for regulated RFPs.

2026-02-12 (Daniel Carter): Evidence request references: do not link to internal restricted folders. Only link to the customer evidence request playbook + the intake channel. Add NDA requirement note for SOC 2 report.

2026-02-18 (Stephanie Nguyen): Sales readiness: request a one-page “How to use the library” plus a reminder to cite version in RFP responses. Also need clarity on who to ping for urgent deal deadlines.

2026-02-21 (Talia Benson): Draft Confluence structure created and populated with 24 blocks. Pending: finalize snippet ID naming convention and confirm owners for quarterly review cadence. Moving to In Review for final sign-off (Security/GRC/Legal).
